items.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: He was coming to my house with his dad for lessons.

ctx.x: If a junior high trombone player saw you play and then came up to you and said, “I want to do what you do.” And his father and mother were standing behind him, do you have advice for that student?

Practice, practice. And stay in school. You know I had a student come to me when I played with Maynard Ferguson in Pittsburgh. Those were always great shows. And his name was Frank Cohen. He walked up to me and said, “I would like to have lessons from you.” I think he was in tenth grade at the time. And he said, “Oh I’d like to have lessons from you.” And I said, “Great, let’s do it. When I’m off the road let’s get together.” So we started getting together. And you know, I don’t see myself as like a teacher in…

a university in Pittsburgh. He was thinking about his options in the region. I said, “Frank, apply to all the best jazz schools on the east coast and just see what happens. He went to the Manhattan School of Music and got a master’s degree. And Frank has several Grammys now. So my advice to him was move to New York. And he did. And he’s doing all this great stuff. And I’m really proud to know him and I’m glad I gave him that advice. Not that he couldn’t have had another path to happiness but it was great to see…
